issues.where: theo:globally_hyperbolic_cauchy_complete_cauchy_maximal, 4th bullet (RamcovGX l.2373–2374; proof l.2390–2395): GX.btzTilde_quotient_homeomorph and the last conjunct of GX.btz_uniformization; REPORT question (i)
issues.problem: The paper endows D(M̃) with 'the BTZ topology in the neighbourhood of the rays' (defi:BTZtop, l.2281: generated by the M³ topology and the sets I⁺(p) ∪ ]p,+∞[ for p on the ray). The PROOF argues the identification with the pushforward topology as a step (l.2390–2395: D(I_{p,q}) = (I⁺(Dp) ∪ D(]p,+∞[)) ∩ I⁻(Dq), 'therefore … generates the BTZ topology on D(M̃)'). The Lean statement instead puts GX.devImageTop d.D on range d.D. That is the M³ subspace topology ⊓ the D-images of T_BTZ-opens, i.e. the T_BTZ topology transported by D. With D injective, D : M̃ → D(M̃) is then a homeomorphism BY CONSTRUCTION (GX.exists_homeomorph_devImageTop). So the 4th bullet, as stated, has no content about the BTZ topology of a subset of 𝐌³; its content is only GX.quotient_virtually_tame plus Galoisness. The step the paper actually proves is neither stated nor proved. This is disclosed: SCOPE (b)(i), REPORT question (i), and the row is partial, so it is not an overclaim. But the dispatch's 'certify IN FULL' is not met, and the gap looks avoidable with the chart tools already in the file. btzTilde_sing_inter_Jplus gives the developed half-line and BTZTildeData.exists_chart_step / chart_notMem_btzJReg_of_sing give the BTZ charts.
issues.fix: Define the BTZ topology on range d.D near the rays per defi:BTZtop: generateFrom of (subspace opens) ∪ {(I⁺(p) ∪ {p + λu, λ>0}) ∩ D(M̃) : p ∈ ⋃Δₓ}, or the l.2392 form with ∩ I⁻(q). Prove it equals devImageTop d.D. For ⊇: rem:tamifying_topology_generated_open with the D(I_{p,q}) computation in a causally convex chart. For ⊆: each generator is a D-image of a T_BTZ-open, plus the subspace part. Then state btzTilde_quotient_homeomorph with that topology. Otherwise the author rules reading (i) accepted, and the row then CLOSES.

issues.where: theo, 4th bullet 'isomorphism M → ρ\D(M̃)' (l.2374; proof l.2397 'isomorphism of singular E-manifolds'); REPORT question (ii)
issues.problem: The headline proves two separate facts: a homeomorphism h : ρ(Γ)\D(M̃) ≃ₜ M, and, in block 1, a local isometry f : Reg M ≃ₜ B onto some GH presentation B of ρ(Γ)\Ω⁺. Nothing in the statement says that h, restricted to the regular classes, is f⁻¹ composed with B's identification. So the 'induced by D' compatibility of the two is not recorded, even though both are [D e] ↦ p(e) by construction. This is a reading question that DEC-87 (c) answered for the twin remark, and it is disclosed.
issues.fix: Optionally add the compatibility conjunct: for e regular, h [D e] = p(e) and f(p(e)) = π(D e), with the same D. Or let the author accept reading (ii).

issues.where: REPORT question (iii) / SCOPE (b)(iii): the rays indexed by BTZ points
issues.problem: This is not a weakening, and asking about it understates what is proved. The headline's third bullet is existential: 'there exists a Γ-invariant family of relatively open future complete lightlike rays (Δᵢ) … such that D(M̃) = (⋃Δᵢ) ∪ ⋂I⁺(Πⱼ)' (DEC-28's display). The Lean witness family (Δₓ)_{x BTZ} satisfies every property: each Δₓ = {Dx + λu, λ>0} is relatively open in its null line, future complete and lightlike; the set of rays is ρ(Γ)-invariant; and the union identity holds. The paper's D(S_x) is the proof's choice of witness, not part of the statement.
issues.fix: Turn question (iii) into a finding: the existential statement is met by a different witness family. The maximal-component family D(S_x) can be added later if wanted.

questions_for_author: Reading (i): accept GX.devImageTop d.D (the T_BTZ topology transported by the injective D) as 'the BTZ topology on D(M̃) in the neighbourhood of the rays'? Or require the identification with defi:BTZtop's generators I⁺(p) ∪ ]p,+∞[, which the proof argues at l.2390–2395? Under acceptance, the headline row closes. Otherwise one more package is owed.
Reading (ii): accept 'isomorphism' as homeomorphism plus the isometry Reg M ≅ ρ(Γ)\Ω⁺, as DEC-87 (c) does for rem:quotient_virtually_tame?

The prop's s ≥ 1: is DEC-77's corrected 'π₁ non-abelian' to be read as DEC-76's finite type, which includes s ≥ 1? With ¬metabelian alone, s = 0 is not excluded: the time reversal of a closed-surface Mess spacetime is past complete. With DEC-119's 'free', s ≥ 1 follows from Cauchy-compactness only via surface classification, which DEC-119 excludes. The file assumes s ≥ 1 explicitly; recording it in the ledger would remove any doubt about the CLOSED mark.
